title: Inventory reconciliation changes the documented skipped-test counting contract
reasoning: CorrectnessResults explicitly excludes skipped tests from aggregate totals, and tests assert that skips do not fail core-cases. Inventory reconciliation instead counts every merged test, including skips. Consequently, applying a complete inventory can change an otherwise identical report's policy result without any missing tests or infrastructure failure.
reproduction: Create results containing one passed Core test and one skipped Core test using add_test_result. core-cases passes initially; apply a matching collection inventory and it fails because the Core total changes from one to two.
recommendation: Centralize aggregate counting so reconciliation preserves the established skipped-test semantics. If strict assessment requires different semantics, express that explicitly in the policy rather than making it depend on the execution path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The report tests verify skip semantics before reconciliation; the supplied collection tests do not apply an inventory to mixed-status results.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend mixed-status report scenarios to apply a complete collection inventory and assert unchanged aggregate counts and policy outcomes across all groups.
minimumFixScope: Inventory aggregate recomputation and report/collection integration coverage.

history.reasoning: All original evidence paths still exist. collection.py:522-528 now excludes skipped tests from aggregate counts, matching report.py:323-347. collection_test.py:129-136 also asserts that a reconciled skipped test contributes zero counts. The code supports an apparent repair, but targeted pytest validation failed before collection because the read-only environment has no writable temporary directory; the mixed-status reproduction also could not start.
